questions.knowledge_point: Computing a Definite Integral Using Integration by Parts
questions.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=2 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x) & ⇒ & v=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 2x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =2x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\cdot 2\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x){|}_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}-{\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x){|}_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(x){|}_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2} \\  & =2[\frac{3\pi }{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2})-\frac{\pi }{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})] \\  & +2[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})] \\  & =2[-\frac{3\pi }{2}-\frac{\pi }{2}]+2[0-0] \\  & =2(-2\pi )+0 \\  & =-4\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing a Trigonometric Expression
questions.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 3x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 3x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =3x\cdot (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3})-\int (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3})\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing a Trigonometric Expression
questions.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int x{csc}^{2}⁡x\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}={csc}^{2}⁡x\, & ⟹\,v=-\operatorname{cot}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot {csc}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot (-\operatorname{cot}⁡x)-\int (-\operatorname{cot}⁡x)\cdot 1\,\text{d}x \\  & =-x\operatorname{cot}⁡x+\int \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral using the substitution $u=\operatorname{sin}⁡x,$ where $\text{d}u=\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{csc}^{2}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =-x\operatorname{cot}⁡x+\int \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-x\operatorname{cot}⁡x+\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-x\operatorname{cot}⁡x+\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =-x\operatorname{cot}⁡x+\operatorname{ln}⁡|\operatorname{sin}⁡x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Computing a Definite Integral Using Integration by Parts
questions.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=9x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=9 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{-3x} & ⇒ & v=-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 9x\cdot {e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x & =9x\cdot (-\frac{{e}^{3x}}{3})-\int (-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3})\cdot 9\,\text{d}x \\  & =-3x{e}^{-3x}+3\int {e}^{-3x}\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1/3}9x{e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x & =-3x{e}^{-3x}{|}_{0}^{1/3}+3{\int }_{0}^{1/3}{e}^{-3x}\text{d}x \\  & =-3x{e}^{-3x}{|}_{0}^{1/3}-{e}^{-3x}{|}_{0}^{1/3} \\  & =-3[\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-3(1/3)}-0\cdot {e}^{-3\cdot 0}]-[{e}^{-3(1/3)}-{e}^{-3\cdot 0}] \\  & =-3[\frac{{e}^{-1}}{3}-0]-[{e}^{-1}-1] \\  & =-\frac{1}{e}-\frac{1}{e}+1 \\  & =1-\frac{2}{e} \\  & =\frac{e-2}{e}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Computing a Definite Integral Using Integration by Parts
questions.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=9x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=9 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{-3x} & ⇒ & v=-\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-3x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 9x\cdot {e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x & =9x\cdot (-\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-3x})-\int (-\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-3x})\cdot 9\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}9x{e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x & =-3x{e}^{-3x}\,{|}_{0}^{1}-3{\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-3x{e}^{-3x}\,{|}_{0}^{1}-{e}^{-3x}\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-3(1\cdot {e}^{-3}-0\cdot {e}^{0})-({e}^{-3}-{e}^{0}) \\  & =-3{e}^{-3}-({e}^{-3}-1) \\  & =1-4{e}^{-3}.\end{aligned}
$$
